  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The tightened finding_id charset validation silently drops valid model-generated findings whose IDs contain characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.

- scripts/security_audit.sh:1376-1378 | severity=blocker | confidence=5

- scripts/security_audit.sh:1519-1526 | severity=blocker | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Deleted-guard ownership analysis inspects only the finding's cited file, missing guard or middleware deletions in other changed files.
  WHY: A guard deleted in `auth.py` while the privileged sink remains unchanged in `views.py` yields an empty cited-file diff, causing blame to classify the sink as base-owned and route the project-introduced bypass to non-blocking advisory findings; severity was reported as MAJOR by moonshotai_kimi-k3 and x-ai_grok-4_6, and BLOCKER by deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro and qwen_qwen3_7-plus.

- scripts/security_audit.sh:1987 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Weekly follow-up deduplication still treats model-generated finding_id as authoritative even when a distinct provenance-bound waiver_match_key exists.
  WHY: A distinct finding whose display ID collides with an existing ai:security issue is skipped and never receives a remediation issue.
